solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: School subject — a thousand MAs teach it badly

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

indicators.note: done badly, the letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A school where a thousand graduates with master's degrees make a poor job of teaching a subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' signals the anagram of MAS TEACH IT, giving ATHEMATICS after the M.
explanation.definitionFit: Maths is a core subject on every school timetable, the study of number and shape.

clue.text: Maiden lands on messy heap, a splodge?

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a maiden is an unmarried young woman, a miss

indicators.note: a messy heap has its letters in disorder

explanation.surface: A girl falls onto an untidy pile and leaves a blot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messy' shuffles HEAP into HAPE, placed under MISS.
explanation.definitionFit: A splodge is an irregular, shapeless blob, so it can be called a deformed form; the question mark flags the loose example.

clue.text: The empty equine facility that may be tried out

indicators.note: an empty word keeps only its outside letters, the inside removed

parts.note: horses are housed in a stable

explanation.surface: An empty horse barn that might be put to the test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves TE from The.
explanation.definitionFit: Something checkable is able to be put to trial, exactly what the adjective expresses.

clue.text: Went wrong, mostly heading north to find Irish town

indicators.note: in a down entry, going north means reading upwards
most of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: to go wrong morally is to have sinned

explanation.surface: A traveller who took a wrong turn and headed north ends up in a town in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts SINNED to SINNE; 'heading north' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennis is the county town of County Clare in the west of Ireland.

clue.text: Adult animal dealt with, in hand

parts.note: A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: letters dealt out like cards end up in a new order

explanation.surface: A grown beast has been handled and is now under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dealt with' shuffles ANIMAL into LAMAIN; the answer is the French phrase meaning by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means done manually, so the English 'in hand' matches its sense of using one's hands.

clue.text: Encouraged at home and mentioned in dispatches?

parts.note: someone at home is in
a soldier mentioned in dispatches is cited for bravery

explanation.surface: A soldier, praised at home and honoured in military reports.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'mentioned in dispatches' is a British military commendation in which an officer's report names a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: To spur someone on or urge them to act is the same as stirring or provoking them.

clue.text: Red Sea apt to be troublesome — what was it for Moses?

indicators.note: letters that are troublesome refuse to stay in order

explanation.surface: The Red Sea is likely to cause difficulty, so what did Moses do to it?
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be troublesome' signals the anagram of RED SEA APT.
explanation.definitionFit: In Exodus the waters of the Red Sea were parted so the Israelites could cross on dry ground.

clue.text: Yawn endlessly in break

indicators.note: with its final letter cut off

parts.note: to yawn is to gape open-mouthed

explanation.surface: A bored yawn that goes on and on during an interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the last letter of GAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A gap is an opening or interruption, a breach in something.

clue.text: Party man turning up by great man

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means reading upwards

parts.note: a stag is the man at a stag party, a groom's pre-wedding night out
taken as written

explanation.surface: A partygoer arrives beside an important figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses STAG to GATS. A stag party is the British name for a bachelor party. The definition alludes to Fitzgerald's novel The Great Gatsby.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitzgerald's title character is called 'The Great' in the novel's name, so he is the great man.

clue.text: Promise to give office assistant part to play

parts.note: PA is short for personal assistant
an actor's part is a role

explanation.surface: A pledge to give a secretary a part in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner released early gives their word of honour to behave, so the word means a pledge.

clue.text: Woman given directions to cross America

indicators.note: the two directions straddle the country, so it goes between them

parts.note: S and N are the compass directions south and north
USA is the United States of America

explanation.surface: A woman is told how to travel across the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cross' puts USA between S and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Susan is a common female first name, an example of a woman.

clue.text: Family of birds in flying practice across island

indicators.note: the shuffled practice letters reach across the island, enclosing it
letters flying about land in a new order

explanation.surface: Birds take flying lessons over an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' shuffles PRACTICE; 'across' puts it round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Accipiter is the genus of hawks such as the goshawk and sparrowhawk, a group of birds of prey.

clue.text: Principal's sharp to gain initial advantage

parts.note: a school principal is the head, so principal's is head's
a sharp taste is tart

explanation.surface: A headteacher with a sharp tongue gains the upper hand early.
explanation.definitionFit: A start ahead of rivals is a lead given at the beginning, an early edge.

clue.text: Bishop in dance is an unconventional type

indicators.note: the bishop's letter goes inside the dance

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop who joins in a dance is a nonconformist.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebel defies authority or convention, so is a nonconformist.

clue.text: Priest about to enter vessel — a good catcher of fish

indicators.note: the priest and the about go into the vessel

parts.note: a pan is a cooking vessel
Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel, a crossword favourite
C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A priest climbs into a boat and proves good at fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: The pelican scoops up fish in its large throat pouch, a skilled fishing bird.

clue.text: Covering domestic animal, worrying about it

indicators.note: the worrying word goes round the domestic animal's word

parts.note: to worry over something is to care, so worrying is caring
a pet is an animal kept in the home

explanation.surface: A pet owner fusses over how to cover their animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is only a pronoun pointing back to the domestic animal; caring is a looser sense of worrying, as in worrying about someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpeting is floor covering, the material laid over a floor.

clue.text: Dirty son avoiding obligation

indicators.note: the word does without the son

parts.note: covered in dust is dirty
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A grubby son shirks his responsibilities.
explanation.definitionFit: A duty is something one is bound to do, a moral or legal requirement.

clue.text: Team benefactor, unnamed, making anything but a grand entrance

parts.note: a side is a sports team

indicators.note: N is short for name, which the word loses

parts.note: a donor gives money, a benefactor

explanation.surface: A club's anonymous sponsor arrives without fanfare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unnamed' removes N (name) from DONOR, leaving DOOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesser entrance at the side of a building is the opposite of a grand front portal.

clue.text: Ornament of twisted nickel, not one that's brilliant

indicators.note: twisted metal is bent out of its shape, so its letters change order
the letter for one is left out

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
ace means excellent, brilliant

explanation.surface: A piece of jewellery made of twisted nickel, which is not a brilliant gem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not one' removes I from NICKEL; 'twisted' turns NCKEL into NECKL.
explanation.definitionFit: A necklace is jewellery worn around the throat, an adornment.

clue.text: Support for piano

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

explanation.surface: A stand for a piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A prop is a support holding something up.

clue.text: Component of eg love drink recipe included

indicators.note: the recipe's letter is taken into the drink

parts.note: a love potion is one kind of magic drink
R is the abbreviation for recipe on prescriptions

explanation.surface: An ingredient of a love philtre, with the recipe enclosed.
explanation.walkthrough: R, from Latin recipe, heads a doctor's prescription.
explanation.definitionFit: A portion is a part or share of a whole.

clue.text: Communist policy to establish impassable boundary

parts.note: red is the colour of communism
a party line is its policy

explanation.surface: A communist party sets out a policy to fix a border no one may cross.
explanation.definitionFit: A limit that must not be crossed, as in a negotiating limit or a gauge's danger mark.

clue.text: Country with retreating soldiers, a sort of madness

indicators.note: retreating soldiers go backwards

parts.note: OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers
mania is a form of mental derangement

explanation.surface: A nation whose troops fall back in a fit of frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns OR into RO.
explanation.definitionFit: Romania is a nation in south-eastern Europe.

clue.text: Sounded very old and very cold?

parts.note: iced means chilled hard

explanation.surface: Someone who seemed very old and chilly.
explanation.definitionFit: To give utterance to something is to express it in words, to say it.

clue.text: Sign of holiness in sergeant major's greeting

indicators.note: the halo goes inside the sergeant major's letters

parts.note: SM is the abbreviation for sergeant major
a halo marks a saint in paintings

explanation.surface: A saintly glow shows in the way a sergeant major says hello.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrew word for peace is used as a salutation both on meeting and parting.

clue.text: Colour of old bit of work with middle missing

indicators.note: the central letter of the five-letter word is taken out and goes to the front, standing for old

parts.note: a chore is a task, a piece of work

explanation.surface: The shade of an old piece of art with a hole in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: The O lifted from the middle of CHORE is set at the front, where it doubles as the usual abbreviation for 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy yellow-brown pigment and the shade named after it.

clue.text: Cooked food upset Mark unfortunately

indicators.note: things gone wrong leave the letters in a muddle

explanation.surface: The meal disappointed a man called Mark, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' signals the anagram of UPSET MARK.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut of beef from the hindquarters, usually grilled or fried, is a meal dish.

clue.text: American place with trading event attracting millions

parts.note: a sale is an occasion for selling goods
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: An American town where a sale brings in millions.
explanation.definitionFit: Salem, Massachusetts, famous for its witch trials, is a town in the United States.

clue.text: Accident, one by holy hill to the east of Scottish island

indicators.note: in an across entry, east of means following

parts.note: Coll is an island in the Inner Hebrides
I is the Roman numeral one
Sion, or Zion, is the hill of Jerusalem

explanation.surface: A mishap by a sacred hill east of a Hebridean island.
explanation.definitionFit: A crash between vehicles is the typical accident in which two things strike each other.

clue.text: An idiot knocked over something in the bathroom

indicators.note: knocked over, the words are read backwards

parts.note: an gives A
a fool is an idiot

explanation.surface: A clumsy fool topples something in the bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' reverses A FOOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A loofah is a dried gourd used as a scrubbing sponge at bath time.

clue.text: Mother and man in garden heading off

indicators.note: the first letter is cut off

parts.note: Adam was the first man, in the garden of Eden

explanation.surface: Mum and a man in the garden set off ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' drops the A of ADAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A dam is the female parent of an animal, especially a horse.

clue.text: Greedier man brought under control with force in France

indicators.note: the unruly letters are brought into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A greedy man is arrested by police in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought under control' signals the anagram of GREEDIER MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The French national police corps, part of the armed forces, is known as this body.
